title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken

items: 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ lb total), sliced in half horizontally to make 4 thin cutlets
2 Tbsp olive oil (or oil from the sun-dried tomato jar)
⅓ cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
12 oz pasta, cooked, or 1 loaf crusty bread, sliced

steps: Pat the cutlets dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the cutlets 3–4 min per side, until golden and they read 165°F in the thickest part. Work in 2 batches if they don't fit with space between them. Move them to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to the same pan and cook 1 min, stirring, until fragrant.
Pour in the cream, add the Italian seasoning and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer gently 3 min, until it thickens slightly.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the parmesan until melted. Add the spinach and stir 1–2 min, until wilted.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Spoon the sauce over it and warm 1–2 min. Serve over pasta, or with bread for the sauce.
tips: If the cutlets are uneven, pound the thick end to ½ inch so they cook evenly.
Add the parmesan over low heat. If the cream boils hard after the cheese goes in, the sauce can turn grainy.
Boneless chicken thighs work too. Cook them 5–6 min per side, to 165°F.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a covered skillet over low heat with a splash of milk or broth until the chicken is hot (165°F). Don't freeze; the cream sauce separates.
